newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen's forces take control of Phnom Penh area.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen's forces take control of Phnom Penh area.

text.p: Forces loyal to Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen appeared to be in complete control of the capital and its outskirts on Monday after rival troops abandoned their stronghold west of the city, a Cambodian military intelligence official said.
Forces loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh had pulled out of Tang Krasang base near Phnom Penh's international airport, the official said.
"Today CPP took control, beginning this morning," said the senior military intelligence official loyal to Ranariddh, referring to Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
Another Ranariddh loyalist confirmed that the base had been abandoned. "Everything is over," said senior commander General Tom Sombol.
It was not immediately clear where Ranariddh's men had withdrawn to, but they had abandoned the base overnight, Tom Sombol said.

Troops loyal to Hun Sen were in complete control of Phnom Penh after two days of fighting in the city and its outskirts. The fighting broke out on Saturday after Hun Sen's men moved against positions, including Tang Krasang, which were under Ranariddh's control in the Phnom Penh area.
